verdict: Lend selectively to small and mid rubber growers and processors in Kottayam at record prices, but structure tightly and avoid price-chasing expansion; the data pack gives no score, so the call rests on price and peer evidence.
title: Kottayam rubber & other plantations: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A rubber smallholder converts latex from standing trees into sheet or scrap and sells it to processors and tyre companies; cash arrives in weekly tapping cycles, not harvest lumps.** The tree is the asset, tapping labour is the main running cost, and the grower has almost no pricing power — the Rubber Board's daily RSS-4 quote sets the day's rate. So when a proposal lands, check the holding size, tree age and whether tapping is owner or leased labour; if the labour is leased, ask for the annual replanting and wage schedule.

## Where value and cash sit now
**Value has moved sharply in the grower's favour: RSS-4 touched Rs 271 per kg, the highest ever in the Indian market [3], and Kottayam reported Rs 300 per kg [1].** That is a local price record, not a peer result, and it is recent — treat it as current, not structural. Downstream, the processors show the margin: Tinna Rubber ran 17.1% EBITDA margins on record FY26 volumes [4], Sampann's rubber segment lifted Q1FY27 revenue 27.6% YoY [5], and Apcotex hit 22.28% EBITDA margins with inventory gains [7]. **The cash is in processing and compounding, not in raw latex.**

## What has changed
**The price spike is pulling the whole chain up, and the state is paying attention — the Rubber Board chairman flagged sector problems ahead of a central minister's Kottayam visit [2].** Peer results are strong but they are processors, not growers, and the rating reports are undated: CARE expects better profitability on tea and rubber price increases and higher tapping from FY26-27 as plants mature [8], and sees no major debt-funded capex at Harrisons [9]. **Sources say little specific about Kottayam's own grower balance sheets, so lean on first principles and these peers.**

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue small and mid growers with mature trees and clean title, and processors with compounding or reclaimed-rubber lines.** Avoid new planting loans and anyone borrowing against the current price to expand area. Structure against the daily Rubber Board price with a margin, take monthly tapping and sales statements, and require the buyer's weighment slips. **Take the stock and receivables position every month; if sales volumes fall while price holds, ask why before renewing.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for growers selling trees, skipping tapping, or diverting to unrecorded buyers.** If the daily RSS-4 quote slips below the level at sanction, re-price the drawing power. If a processor's inventory days stretch while margins stay high, that is inventory gain, not demand — ask for the order book.
watch: falls below sanction assumption -> re-price drawing power and pause enhancements
volume falls while price holds -> ask for buyer slips and inspect the holding
stretches with high margins -> treat as inventory gain, seek order book
trees past prime without replanting plan -> cap tenor to remaining tree life
